title: Interaction Gambits — micro-friction flows & token-aware UX (scratch)
content:
Context
— quick brain-dump about lightweight product patterns to reduce per-session token spend while preserving perceived responsiveness and quality.

Problem statement
— apps are under pressure to lower unit cost. Straight token shaving (truncate prompts) often breaks UX. We can design tiny interaction gambits: short micro-turns, progressive fidelity, and explicit micro-confirmations that keep user flow but reduce model compute.

Goal
— prototype 3 small, A/B-testable gambits for chat-style integrations that reduce median tokens-per-session by 10–30% for targeted flows without lowering NPS by >1 point.

User personas
- Product manager (PM) embedding assistant into a CRM: wants predictable monthly costs, no user complaints about missing details.
- Embedded-app end user (sales rep): wants answers fast, tolerates a quick clarifying question but hates full follow-ups.
- Developer on Redwood SDK: wants a control primitive to opt-in/out and telemetry hooks.

Ideas (candidate gambits) — rough descriptions
1) Micro-clarify gambit
   - If model confidence low (heuristic: short context overlap, high p(token) entropy, or explicit classifier), issue a single short clarifying question prompted in-system: "Quick check — do you want only the top-level summary or full context?"
   - default = top-level summary, can expand on user request.
   - Expected token savings: 20–40% on long-document summarization flows.
   - Failure modes: user hates extra clicks; conversation fragmentation.

2) Progressive fidelity ladder
   - Return a tiny (1–3 sentence) capsule first, streamed; if user clicks "More" or waits X seconds, then generate full response at higher model/setting.
   - Implementation: two-step generation (cheap-mode then high-fidelity fallback). Can use smaller model for capsule.
   - Metrics: conversion-to-more, extra-token delta, latency impact.

3) Token-aware follow-up compression
   - When user asks multi-part question, compress follow-ups into numbered micro-answers (bullets) instead of verbose prose. Provide "Expand 2" buttons to fetch full text for item 2 on demand.
   - Use templated compressions with optional 'expand' hooks that call runtime with KV cache to restore context cheaply.

Instrumentation / telemetry (what we need)
- Gambit invoked (bool), gambit_type, pre_tokens_estimate, post_tokens_actual, model_used_primary, model_used_secondary, user_action (expand/confirm/ignore), session_id, latency_ms_primary, latency_ms_secondary, satisfaction_signal (thumbs up/down), churn_event within 24h.
- Important derived metrics: tokens_saved_per_session, percent_sessions_with_gambit, expand-rate, NPS-delta, revenue impact estimate.

Product primitives to build (developer-facing)
- low-friction gambit SDK: declarative config: trigger_rules (confidence thresholds + heuristics), primary_generator (model|params), secondary_generator, fallback_policy, prompt_templates, client_ui_hints (button labels), ttl for cached expansions.
- lightweight UI components: capsule-card, expand-button, clarification-tooltips — shipped as React/vanilla snippets for quick prototyping.
- rollout controls: per-route toggles, percentage rollout, canary bucket by customer tier.

Rough API sketch (for engineering convo)
- POST /v1/generate?gambit=progressive_fidelity
  body: {session_id, messages, gambit_hint:{min_confidence:0.7, capsule_model:"redwood-small", full_model:"redwood-medium"}}
- response: {capsule: {text, token_estimate}, expand_id} then client calls /expand/{expand_id} for full.

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- Implementation of 2 gambits (Micro-clarify, Progressive fidelity) in hosted API sandbox.
- SDK flag + telemetry emitted for each gambit event.
- Experiment config UI entry (console) for enabling gambit on single route.
- Initial AB experiment run: 3-week, random 50/50 split on a low-risk internal route (docs-summary).
- Target: >=12% median token reduction; user satisfaction (thumbs-up rate) delta <= -1% absolute.

Experiment design notes
- Start internal-first: docs team + a handful of internal customers. Use synthetic workload too.
- Guardrail: auto-disable if expand-rate < 1% and satisfaction drops >2 points.

Open questions / unknowns
- Signal for "low confidence" at runtime — do we expose model logits? Or build a lightweight classifier trained on prior generations?
- Pricing implications: do we bill capsule + expand separately, or attribute tokens to customer usage naturally? Need finance input.
- KV cache cost for on-demand expansions — small perf cost but important for economics.
- UX: how intrusive are clarifying gambits on mobile? Need prototype testing.
- Compliance/data residency: expansions may happen in other region if fallback model chosen; tie to routing policy.

Implementation risks
- Extra complexity in runtime path (two-step generation) increases surface area for outages.
- Telemetry cardinality explosion if we track every micro-action — need careful event design.

Next steps (short runbook)
1) Proto week (2 engineers + PM + designer): ship a console toggle + SDK hook + server-side capsule generator for 1 route.
2) UX quick mock + prototype on mobile and desktop. 1 designer sprint.
3) Instrumentation: events + dashboard sketch (tokens saved, expand-rate, satisfaction).
4) Run internal AB for 3 weeks; collect metrics and notes.
5) Decision: iterate / roll to beta customers / scrap.

Notes-to-self (todo)
- Talk to Noah about telemetry quota impacts (ticket JIRA-OBS-901).
- Ping Finance re: billing model for multi-stage requests.
- Draft copy for console toggle help text: "Enable micro-gambits: small UX tweaks that reduce token use by returning short capsules; can be toggled route-by-route."
- Prototype capsule UI as a compact card with 3-dot menu to request full.

Quick mocks I want to sketch in Figma
- Capsule card mobile vs desktop
- Clarify micro-modal copy variants (3 options)
- Expand flow micro-animation (progressive reveal)

Slack traces / references (for context)
- #product-experiments: conversation re: progressive fidelity (Feb 18)
- #runtime-costs: notes from ops on token billing edge-cases

End of scratch.

Random rough thought: combine gambits with per-session QoS lanes (cheap capsule on low QoS, full on high). Could tie to subscription tiers as advantage feature.

-- EY (quick notes)
